segments.t: Something is wrong in the kitchen: the big stove has disappeared. Senya, the meat cook, wants to know where it has gone, and Barinov has an answer ready. Listen first, and I'll explain afterwards.
Шеф, куда пропала наша большая плита?
Я лично отвёз её в надёжный сервис.
Но она отлично работала вчера вечером!
Я сдал её для важной профилактики.
А на чём нам готовить сегодня?
Пока готовьте блюда на этой плитке.
Эта маленькая плитка нагревается слишком медленно!
Хватит ныть, повара должны уметь всё!
Гости будут очень долго ждать заказы!
Поставьте нагрев на четвёрку и работайте!
Когда нам вернут нашу старую плиту?
Через день или два всё привезут!
Let's unpack it.
Шеф, куда пропала наша большая плита?
пропала

'Chef, where has our big stove disappeared to?' They express 'where' by implies direction, and this word is "vanished", with a she-word ending because They express 'stove' by is a she-word word. Senya sees an empty space.
Я лично отвёз её в надёжный сервис.
отвёз
'I personally took it to a reliable repair service.' This word is "took away" by vehicle, not on foot. We hear 'reliable' grows from We hear 'hope', and the first word means "personally".
Но она отлично работала вчера вечером!
вчера
вечером

'But it was working perfectly yesterday evening!' This phrase is "yesterday in the evening": When they say 'evening' takes an instrumental ending. The stove is "she" in Russian, so When they say 'worked' takes a she-word ending.
Я сдал её для важной профилактики.
профилактики

'I turned it in for important preventive maintenance.' The second word is "handed in". This word, prophylaxis, is a doctor's word Russians also use for servicing machines. It sounds impressive, and that's why he uses it.
А на чём нам готовить сегодня?
на
чём
'And on what are we to cook today?' Russians cook "on" a stove, so it's this phrase, "on what". In Russian, 'are we to cook' translates literally translates to "to us to cook". Senya is practical.
Пока готовьте блюда на этой плитке.
плитке

'For now cook the dishes on this little hotplate.' Here, 'for now' shows is also used for "while" and "bye". This word is the word for stove with a diminutive ending, meaning a little hotplate. The command to cook is addressed to the whole kitchen.
Эта маленькая плитка нагревается слишком медленно!
нагревается

'This little hotplate heats up much too slowly!' This The way to express 'heats up' has a self-directed ending, meaning "heats itself". The following words mean "too" and "slowly". Senya complains, and he has every right.
Хватит ныть, повара должны уметь всё!
Хватит
ныть

'Stop whining, cooks must know how to do everything!' This phrase uses "enough" as common speech for "stop it", followed by the action word "to whine". 'must know how' is used here uses a action 'to be able' is used here, indicating a skill.
Гости будут очень долго ждать заказы!
заказы
'The guests will wait for their orders very long!' Listen to how 'will wait' is made from "will be" plus the dictionary form. This word is "orders", the multiple form.
Поставьте нагрев на четвёрку и работайте!
четвёрку

'Set the heat to four and get to work!' The sentence says "put the heating on a four": this word is the number four as a thing word, which is also a school mark. The commands to put and to work are addressed to everyone.
Когда нам вернут нашу старую плиту?
нашу
старую
плиту

'When will they return our old stove to us?' The action word is "they will return", with no one named. This phrase ends with accusative markers three times, because the stove is being returned. Senya knows there's no answer.
Через день или два всё привезут!
привезут

'In a day or two they will bring everything!' We hear 'in a day' literally means "through a day". This word is "will bring" by vehicle, similar to We hear 'took away'. Barinov's plan depends on nobody checking. Back to the full version.

The stove is gone, and the kitchen is cooking on a toy. Barinov says it will be back in a day or two. We'll see how that goes. Take care until then.
